macro_themes.stance_summary: Chamath argues AI will create 9-10 vertically integrated mega-corps from dirt to apps; the group agrees industries will be rewritten.
Chamath and Jason argue acquisitions beat buybacks in a disruption era; Jason sees a limited political window for big M&A.
Anthropic's record $2T IPO drew massive demand; Friedberg is bullish long term, Chamath says near-term valuation depends on macro.
Chamath sees sticky inflation as a key headwind for equities.
Chamath expects a rising 10-year and little room for Warsh to cut, possibly a hike.
The AI job-apocalypse narrative is dismissed; new frontier jobs outpace losses, though a K-shaped backlash is a risk.
All three oppose the reported open source disclosure rule; Friedberg calls curbs on open source a path to tyranny.
China hawks are gaining influence; the hosts debate whether Chinese open models really advantage China and note Nvidia ended H200 China sales.
Hosts lament the lack of a competitive US open source model, blaming incentives and capital flows to closed frontier labs.
On Jensen's ouster, Chamath says reinstatement won't happen and urges waiting for hearings; Friedberg won't trust media; Jason speculates on rogue resellers.
